title: Sensex Falls 489 Points as Infosys Guidance Cut and Oil Hit Markets
excerpt: The Nifty slipped below 22,500 on Monday, October 26, as Infosys cut fiscal 2027 growth guidance to 1%-2%, Brent crude held near $110 and investors waited for the Federal Reserve decision.
body:
• The Sensex fell 489 points to 72,635 and the Nifty dropped 186 points to 22,413 by 9:24 a.m. on Monday, October 26, after opening more than 400 points lower.
  • Infosys fell about 3% after cutting its fiscal 2027 constant-currency revenue growth guidance to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, its weakest forecast in seven years.
  • Brent crude near $110 a barrel after attacks on Saudi facilities and caution before the Federal Reserve meeting on October 27-28 added to the selling.
  • For diaspora investors holding Indian IT stocks: Infosys closed Friday at Rs 1,153.80, down 28.2% in 2026; UBS kept a Buy with a Rs 1,415 target while HSBC held with Rs 1,110.

Indian equities opened sharply lower on Monday, October 26, with the BSE Sensex down 489 points at 72,635 and the NSE Nifty 50 down 186 points at 22,413 as of 9:24 a.m., according to Upstox market data. The Sensex fell as much as 574 points in early trade and the Nifty touched an intraday low of 22,397, breaching the 22,500 level. Selling was broad: 2,033 shares fell against 1,077 advancing on the NSE, the Nifty Midcap 100 dropped 0.84% and the Smallcap 100 fell 1.26%.

Infosys guidance cut leads the decline

Infosys was the largest drag. Shares fell 2.7% in early trading after the company cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1%-2% from 1.5%-3%, Reuters reported, noting that most analysts had expected only a trim of the upper end to 2.5%. Reuters cited weakness in Infosys's North America business. The company reported second-quarter net profit up 6.2% year on year to Rs 7,823 crore and revenue up 10.7% to Rs 49,244 crore, but operating profit of Rs 10,330 crore missed expectations and operating margin slipped 10 basis points sequentially to 21%. Infosys kept its margin guidance at 20%-22%.

There were offsets inside the result. Large deal wins rose to $5.2 billion from $3.6 billion in the first quarter, with 62% net-new business, and AI services revenue grew 29% sequentially to 10.5% of total revenue. Brokerages split on what follows: UBS maintained a Buy rating with a target of Rs 1,415, about 23% above Friday's close of Rs 1,153.80, while HSBC kept a Hold with a target of Rs 1,110 and warned that wage hikes could pressure second-half margins. Systematix called it a disappointing quarter, citing pricing pressure from AI-driven client productivity demands, and Motilal Oswal pointed to weaker volumes and Infosys's exit from a large European manufacturing contract.

"Disappointing quarter"

— Systematix analysts, on Infosys's second-quarter results

Oil, Shriram Finance and a weak Asia session

Infosys was not the only problem. Shriram Finance was the top Nifty loser, falling nearly 5% to Rs 823 after cutting its assets under management growth guidance to 15%-17% from 18% and warning of higher credit costs, despite a better-than-expected second-quarter profit. ICICI Bank, Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, Bajaj Finance and State Bank of India also weighed on the benchmarks. Sector losses ran from 0.6% to 1.05% across bank, financial services, IT, auto, PSU bank, realty and consumer durables gauges, with FMCG down 1.35%; pharma was the exception. Dr Reddy's Laboratories rose 2.8% to Rs 1,264 after net profit rose 11% to Rs 925 crore, and Kotak Mahindra Bank, JSW Steel and Adani Ports also gained.

External pressure came from energy and Asia. Brent crude futures hovered around $110 a barrel after Houthi attacks on a Saudi airport and oil facilities over the weekend; Saudi Arabia said it intercepted missiles and drones and restarted partial airport operations on Sunday. Japan's Nikkei fell 0.61%, China's Shanghai Composite declined 0.51%, South Korea's KOSPI dropped 1.24% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng slipped 0.06%. The rupee weakened three paise to 94.96 against the US dollar, and gold steadied near $4,000 an ounce.

What investors watch next

The Federal Reserve meets on October 27-28. Markets widely expect rates to stay unchanged, so the focus is on Chair Warsh's comments on a possible December move and on the US Personal Consumption Expenditures inflation report. For Indian IT, the question is whether the guidance cut marks a sector floor: Tata Consultancy Services and HCLTech met revenue estimates earlier this month, leaving Infosys as the outlier among the top five. Infosys stock is down 28.2% so far in 2026 against a 13.6% fall in the Nifty 50, with a market capitalisation of about Rs 4.7 lakh crore, so any stabilisation in North American client spending will move both the stock and the index.
